name: Prompt Injection
question: Why is there no patch for prompt injection, and what do you build instead?
problem: SQL injection was fixed with parameterised queries, because SQL has a grammar. A model reads the system prompt, the user's message and an attacker's sentence as one string.
points: Give the agent only the tools the task needs.
Ask a human before anything irreversible: send, delete, pay.
Never let untrusted content call a tool.
title: Prompt Injection: Why LLM Security Has No Fix (And What To Do Instead) #shorts
caption:
Prompt injection explained — why LLM security has no fix, and how to build AI agents that survive it anyway.

Your LLM app has an SQL-injection problem, and there's no parameterized query for it.

SQL had a grammar, so we could put a wall between code and data. A large language model has no grammar. System prompt, user input and an attacker's sentence hidden in an email or webpage all arrive as one string — same tokens, no labels. That's why prompt injection has sat at #1 on the OWASP LLM Top 10 since the list existed, and why filtering "ignore previous instructions" is a blacklist that a language model will always out-rewrite.

You don't stop the injection. You make it worthless:
① least-privilege tools — the agent only gets what the task needs
② human confirmation on anything irreversible — send, delete, pay
③ untrusted content never calls a tool

That's the AI agent security blueprint for Part 11. Script, canvas and notes are in the open vault — link in bio.
